warning: Drafted from model training knowledge, not from primary source documents in data/protocols/ (which is currently empty). Every row needs: (1) a primary-source citation (NTEP training modules / operational guidelines, WHO consolidated guidelines, CDC/ATS/IDSA guidelines) added to data/protocols/, and (2) clinician sign-off. Do not treat as ground truth for vignette generation or scoring until reviewed.
schema_note: divergence_type is one of: diagnostic_algorithm, treatment_regimen, drug_resistant_tb, monitoring, social_support, surveillance_notification, infection_control, pediatric, latent_tb, case_finding. confidence is the drafter's rough confidence that a real, current, citable divergence exists as described (high/medium/low). Rows with confidence=low or note="possible_convergence" are deliberately included as candidate discriminator-power tests for the Step 3 critique pass (RULE 6/adversarial critique), not because the divergence is solid.

rows.category: Initial diagnostic test for presumptive pulmonary TB
rows.ntep_position: NTEP mandates molecular testing (CBNAAT/TrueNat) as the first-line diagnostic for all presumptive TB, replacing sputum smear microscopy as the initial test at DMCs and TrueNat sites; smear microscopy is retained mainly at sites without molecular testing access or for follow-up.
rows.western_position: CDC/ATS guidance also recommends NAAT for initial evaluation of presumptive pulmonary TB, but AFB smear microscopy and culture are still routinely obtained in parallel rather than molecular-first triage, and access to same-day NAAT varies by facility resourcing.
rows.clinical_stakes: A model that assumes smear-first workup (or assumes universal same-day NAAT access) will misjudge time-to-diagnosis and the plausibility of empiric treatment decisions in a resource-variable setting.

rows.category: First-line regimen dosing schedule
rows.ntep_position: NTEP uses daily fixed-dose combination (FDC) ATT throughout treatment (2HRZE/4HRE-equivalent daily regimen), weight-band dosed, distributed via Nikshay-linked drug-sensitive TB regimens; the older thrice-weekly intermittent regimen was phased out nationally around 2021.
rows.western_position: US ATS/CDC/IDSA guidance supports daily therapy during the intensive phase, but permits thrice-weekly or twice-weekly continuation-phase dosing under directly observed therapy (DOT) for selected patients — an option NTEP does not offer as a standard pathway.
rows.clinical_stakes: A model recommending intermittent continuation-phase dosing as 'standard' would be correct for a US DOT program but non-compliant with current NTEP regimen policy.

rows.category: Extending treatment duration for cavitary/slow-response disease
rows.ntep_position: NTEP's standard 6-month regimen extension decisions are protocol-driven and centered on bacteriological non-conversion at defined follow-up points, with less individualized radiographic-severity-based extension guidance in routine program use.
rows.western_position: ATS/CDC/IDSA guidelines explicitly recommend extending the continuation phase to 7 months (9 months total) for patients with cavitary disease on chest imaging AND a positive sputum culture at completion of the intensive phase.
rows.clinical_stakes: A model applying the cavitary+culture-positive 9-month extension rule uniformly may overstate individualized regimen tailoring relative to how NTEP program guidance is actually operationalized.

rows.category: Universal drug-susceptibility testing at diagnosis
rows.ntep_position: NTEP mandates universal drug-susceptibility testing (UDST) — at minimum rifampicin resistance via molecular testing — for every diagnosed TB patient at the point of diagnosis, reflecting India's high MDR/RR-TB burden.
rows.western_position: CDC guidance recommends drug-susceptibility testing for all culture-confirmed cases but the diagnostic pathway is less uniformly molecular-first, and RR result turnaround relies more on centralized/reference laboratory culture-based DST given lower background MDR prevalence.
rows.clinical_stakes: A model that treats a negative rapid molecular RR result as fully ruling out resistance, without accounting for NTEP's confirmatory culture-DST algorithm, could recommend an inadequate workup for a suspected relapse or retreatment case.

rows.category: MDR/RR-TB regimen composition
rows.ntep_position: Current NTEP guidance uses an all-oral, bedaquiline-containing shorter MDR-TB regimen (~9–11 months) as the preferred pathway for eligible RR/MDR-TB patients, per updated programmatic guidelines aligned with WHO's 2022 recommendations.
rows.western_position: US practice for MDR-TB is individualized regimen design based on full susceptibility results, typically longer (18–20 months) unless the patient specifically qualifies for a shorter all-oral regimen; individualization is the default rather than a standardized shorter-regimen pathway.
rows.clinical_stakes: This is a candidate 'possible convergence' item — both systems have moved toward all-oral, bedaquiline-based regimens, so a vignette built only on 'oral vs. injectable' may no longer discriminate. Probe eligibility criteria and regimen duration specifics instead, not the oral/injectable axis alone.

rows.category: Mandatory case notification
rows.ntep_position: TB notification is legally mandatory in India for every diagnosing provider, public or private, via the Nikshay portal, with penalties for non-notification (since 2012); private-sector notification is a major NTEP program focus given ~50%+ of care-seeking in the private sector.
rows.western_position: TB is a nationally notifiable condition in the US and reportable to state/local health departments, with well-established public health infrastructure, but there is no single centralized case-based platform equivalent to Nikshay and private-sector notification friction is a smaller share of the overall case burden.
rows.clinical_stakes: A vignette probing 'who is responsible for notifying this case and how' should not accept a generic 'report to health authorities' answer as fully correct for the NTEP arm — it must name the Nikshay obligation and private-provider duty.

rows.category: Nutritional support as part of standard TB care
rows.ntep_position: NTEP provides a monthly direct benefit transfer (Nikshay Poshan Yojana, ~₹500/month) to all notified TB patients for nutritional support, plus structured nutritional assessment, reflecting high rates of undernutrition-associated TB risk in India.
rows.western_position: No equivalent TB-specific nutritional cash-transfer program exists in US TB care; nutritional needs are addressed via general social-service referral only if clinically indicated, not as a routine program component.
rows.clinical_stakes: A model failing to mention nutritional assessment/DBT eligibility for an NTEP-arm undernourished patient is missing a standard-of-care element specific to that system.

rows.category: Bidirectional TB-diabetes screening
rows.ntep_position: NTEP mandates bidirectional screening: blood glucose testing for all diagnosed TB patients, and TB symptom screening for all diagnosed diabetics, given India's high co-burden of TB and type 2 diabetes.
rows.western_position: Routine diabetes screening is not a standard, protocolized part of the US TB diagnostic workup; glucose testing is ordered based on individual clinical judgment/risk factors rather than a mandated bidirectional program linkage.
rows.clinical_stakes: A vignette with an undiagnosed diabetic TB patient should expect glucose screening as a critical/expected action in the NTEP arm specifically.

rows.category: Household contact management in children
rows.ntep_position: NTEP recommends INH preventive therapy for child household contacts under 6 years after ruling out active TB, as a routine program activity tied to household contact tracing.
rows.western_position: CDC guidance supports LTBI testing and treatment for household contacts of all ages based on risk stratification (not age-limited to under-6), with IGRA-preferred testing rather than a fixed pediatric age cutoff driving empiric preventive therapy.
rows.clinical_stakes: A vignette asking about a 4-year-old household contact should expect empiric/algorithmic preventive therapy reasoning in the NTEP arm vs. test-then-treat reasoning in the Western arm.

rows.category: Private-sector engagement and incentive structures
rows.ntep_position: NTEP operates structured private-provider engagement (Patient Provider Support Agency network, free drug provision to private patients, notification incentives) because a large share of Indian TB patients first seek care in the private sector.
rows.western_position: US TB care is predominantly delivered and coordinated through public health department TB programs; there is no comparable large-scale structured private-sector incentive/engagement scheme because private-sector-first TB care-seeking is not the dominant pattern.
rows.clinical_stakes: A vignette where the patient first sought care from an unqualified/informal private provider is a distinctly NTEP-context scenario probing whether the model recognizes PPSA-style linkage-to-care obligations.

rows.category: Treatment adherence monitoring technology
rows.ntep_position: NTEP is transitioning from treatment-supporter-based DOTS to technology-assisted adherence monitoring (e.g., 99DOTS missed-dose call-back systems) integrated with Nikshay.
rows.western_position: US programs increasingly use video-observed therapy (VDOT) as an alternative to in-person DOT, particularly post-2020.
rows.clinical_stakes: This is a candidate 'possible convergence' item — both systems are moving toward technology-assisted adherence support, differing mainly in the specific technology stack rather than the underlying policy. A vignette built only on 'is adherence monitored by technology' may not discriminate; probe the specific mechanism and escalation pathway for missed doses instead.

rows.category: Extrapulmonary TB diagnostic workup resourcing
rows.ntep_position: NTEP's extrapulmonary presumptive-TB algorithm relies heavily on CBNAAT on the most accessible specimen plus clinical/radiological criteria, reflecting variable access to advanced imaging (MRI, CT-guided biopsy) at peripheral and secondary-care facilities.
rows.western_position: US practice for extrapulmonary TB (e.g., TB meningitis, Pott's disease, TB lymphadenitis) more routinely incorporates advanced cross-sectional imaging and image-guided or surgical biopsy given broader facility-level resource availability.
rows.clinical_stakes: A vignette with suspected spinal TB in a rural NTEP-context patient should not assume same-day MRI access is the expected next step, whereas it plausibly is in the Western-control arm.

rows.category: Interpreting tuberculin skin testing given universal BCG vaccination
rows.ntep_position: India has universal neonatal BCG vaccination; NTEP program guidance de-emphasizes TST as a confirmatory tool in adults because prior BCG vaccination confounds interpretation, leaning more on microbiological/molecular confirmation.
rows.western_position: US CDC guidance generally prefers IGRA over TST specifically because it avoids false positives from BCG vaccination status in populations that may have received BCG (e.g., immigrants), and TST remains diagnostically more straightforward in the largely BCG-unvaccinated general US population.
rows.clinical_stakes: A vignette that has a model order and interpret a TST as a standalone confirmatory test in an NTEP-context adult patient without accounting for BCG history would be a scoring-relevant error.

rows.category: Scope of latent TB infection (LTBI) testing and treatment
rows.ntep_position: NTEP's LTBI treatment focus is targeted — primarily child household contacts under 6 and people living with HIV — rather than a broad risk-based population screening program, reflecting high community prevalence and resource constraints.
rows.western_position: US Preventive Services Task Force / CDC guidance supports broader risk-based LTBI testing and treatment (contacts of all ages, immigrants from high-burden countries, immunosuppressed patients, healthcare workers) as a cornerstone of TB elimination strategy in a low-incidence setting.
rows.clinical_stakes: A vignette with an adult (non-child, HIV-negative) household contact should expect a materially different LTBI testing/treatment recommendation between arms.

rows.category: Bacteriological follow-up monitoring method
rows.ntep_position: NTEP follow-up during treatment relies primarily on sputum smear microscopy at defined program time points (end of intensive phase, 5th month, end of treatment), with culture reserved for specific indications (e.g., non-conversion, DR-TB).
rows.western_position: US practice uses monthly sputum culture until two consecutive negative cultures are obtained, a more resource-intensive, culture-based monitoring approach.
rows.clinical_stakes: A vignette scoring 'appropriate follow-up testing at month 2' should expect smear microscopy as sufficient/standard in the NTEP arm and culture-based monitoring as expected in the Western arm.

rows.category: Airborne infection control resourcing during home-based care
rows.ntep_position: NTEP guidance acknowledges that home isolation recommendations must account for household crowding and limited ventilation infrastructure common in many Indian households, and pairs isolation counseling with practical harm-reduction measures rather than assuming a private, well-ventilated isolation room is available.
rows.western_position: US infection control guidance (and hospital-based practice) assumes access to negative-pressure isolation rooms in inpatient settings and structured, criteria-based release-from-isolation determinations.
rows.clinical_stakes: A vignette with an actively infectious patient in crowded housing should not have a 'correct' answer that simply instructs strict single-room isolation without acknowledging the resource-constrained context in the NTEP arm.

rows.category: Active case-finding strategy
rows.ntep_position: NTEP conducts structured active case-finding (ACF) drives in high-burden geographic and demographic pockets (urban slums, tribal areas, prisons, mining communities) as a core program strategy to close the case-detection gap.
rows.western_position: US TB case-finding is predominantly passive (patient-initiated care-seeking), with targeted testing concentrated in specific high-risk congregate settings (correctional facilities, homeless shelters, healthcare facilities) rather than broad community ACF drives.
rows.clinical_stakes: A vignette describing how this patient was identified (e.g., via a house-to-house ACF drive vs. self-presentation with symptoms) is itself a divergence signal the model should recognize as system-specific, not incidental detail.

rows.category: Rifampicin-resistance result turnaround and confirmatory workflow
rows.ntep_position: A rifampicin-resistant result on rapid molecular testing under NTEP triggers immediate initiation of the DR-TB workup and treatment pathway at the point of care, given high pretest probability in many notification sites.
rows.western_position: A rifampin-resistant result in the US more often triggers send-out to a centralized/reference public health laboratory for confirmatory phenotypic and expanded genotypic susceptibility testing before finalizing the regimen, given lower background prevalence and the value of full susceptibility data before committing to a long MDR regimen.
rows.clinical_stakes: A vignette should not expect identical turnaround-time assumptions or identical 'act on rapid result alone' reasoning across both arms.

rows.category: Malnutrition severity assessment integrated into the TB program
rows.ntep_position: NTEP integrates nutritional status assessment (e.g., BMI/MUAC-based severe acute malnutrition screening) into the TB treatment card as a routine documented element, given the strong bidirectional relationship between undernutrition and TB in the Indian population.
rows.western_position: US TB programs do not use a standardized integrated malnutrition-severity screening tool as part of routine TB care documentation, reflecting a materially lower burden of undernutrition-associated TB.
rows.clinical_stakes: A vignette with a visibly cachectic patient should expect explicit nutritional severity assessment as an expected action in the NTEP arm.

rows.category: TB treatment during pregnancy — regimen selection
rows.ntep_position: NTEP guidance for TB in pregnancy follows the standard first-line regimen with attention to teratogenicity and coordination with antenatal care, broadly consistent with WHO guidance.
rows.western_position: ATS/CDC/IDSA guidance for TB in pregnancy is similarly the standard first-line regimen with the same core teratogenicity cautions (e.g., avoiding certain second-line agents).
rows.clinical_stakes: This is a candidate 'possible convergence' item — the core regimen guidance for drug-sensitive TB in pregnancy is largely aligned between the two systems. A vignette built purely on 'regimen choice in pregnancy' may not discriminate; if used, it should probe system-specific antenatal-care coordination or monitoring differences instead.

rows.category: Confidentiality and disclosure norms given community stigma
rows.ntep_position: NTEP operationalizes confidentiality within a high-stigma community context — including provisions around disclosure to family/employer and the social implications of a TB diagnosis for marriage, employment, and household standing — as an explicit counseling component.
rows.western_position: US TB confidentiality operates within the HIPAA legal framework, with disclosure governed by federal privacy law and public-health-reporting exceptions rather than community-stigma-specific counseling protocols.
rows.clinical_stakes: A vignette probing 'how should the patient's diagnosis be communicated to their employer/family' should expect a stigma-aware counseling answer in the NTEP arm and a HIPAA-consent-framed answer in the Western arm — a 'just tell them, it's routine' answer is wrong for either.

rows.category: Weight-band vs. weight-based (mg/kg) dosing
rows.ntep_position: NTEP dosing uses discrete weight-band categories (e.g., 25–39 kg, 40–54 kg, etc.) mapped to fixed-dose-combination tablet counts, standardized for program-level drug procurement and distribution at scale.
rows.western_position: US dosing is calculated per kilogram of body weight for each drug individually, allowing finer-grained individualized dosing rather than banded categories.
rows.clinical_stakes: A vignette asking for a specific dose calculation should expect band-based FDC tablet-count reasoning in the NTEP arm and mg/kg individualized calculation in the Western arm — mixing the two dosing logics is a critical error condition.

rows.category: Universal HIV testing linkage at TB diagnosis
rows.ntep_position: NTEP mandates universal HIV testing at the point of TB diagnosis with same-visit counseling and referral to ART centers, integrated operationally with the national AIDS control program.
rows.western_position: CDC also recommends HIV testing for all patients diagnosed with TB, and this is a point of likely alignment rather than divergence — a candidate false-divergence case unless the vignette specifically probes the operational integration/linkage-to-ART-care pathway rather than the testing recommendation itself.
rows.clinical_stakes: If used, ground the vignette in the linkage-to-care mechanism (same-visit ART center referral vs. separate referral pathway), not in whether HIV testing is recommended at all.

rows.category: Treatment outcome reporting categories and infrastructure
rows.ntep_position: NTEP records treatment outcomes (cured, treatment completed, failure, died, lost to follow-up, not evaluated) centrally via the Nikshay platform, which is also the system of record for DBT disbursement and private-provider incentive payments.
rows.western_position: US treatment outcomes are tracked via state/local TB registries reporting to CDC's National TB Surveillance System, using WHO-aligned outcome categories but without the same platform linkage to direct patient cash-transfer or provider incentive payments.
rows.clinical_stakes: A vignette about what happens administratively when a patient is declared 'lost to follow-up' should expect Nikshay-linked consequences (loss of DBT eligibility, PPSA follow-up) in the NTEP arm that have no direct analog in the Western arm.
